S1.why: Plural adjective after the number, no noun: under the bracket the tiles themselves are the noun. Only right for 2 and above, and the brief fixes this at 5.

S2.why: A plain invitation using the vocab's item word; 'пазя' (keep) is the save verb in every key on this sheet. 19 characters.

S3.s: Използвахте всичките %lld безплатни Кътлинга. Те си остават безплатни и работят както досега.
S3.back: You-used all-the 5 free Cutlings. They themselves remain free and work as until-now.
S3.why: Formal 'вие' as in the vocab sentence. 'Кътлинга' is the count form a masculine noun takes after a number. 'Си остават' says they simply stay as they are, with no hint of anything taken away.

S4.why: Count form after the number, and the same verb as the title.

S5.why: 'X от Y' is how Bulgarian says X of Y. The noun follows the 5, so the count form is right whatever the first number is. Positional placeholders keep the order explicit.

S6.why: A noun phrase as a row head, the way Bulgarian feature rows read. Count form after the number. 23 characters with the number.

S7.s: До %@ текстови Кътлинга и до %lld изображения.
S7.back: Up-to 5 000 text Cutlings and up-to 500 images.
S7.why: 'Текстови Кътлинга' comes from the vocab's 'Текстов Кътлинг'. 'Изображения' is the vocab's word for images. 'До' is repeated because the two limits are separate.

S8.why: A Bulgarian list puts no comma before 'и'. Apple device names stay in Latin script, as the vocab writes 'Mac'.

S9.s: Една покупка важи за всички устройства с вашия Apple акаунт.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid for all devices with your Apple account.
S9.why: 'Важи за' is the everyday phrase for a purchase or ticket that covers something. 'Вашия Apple акаунт' is taken word for word from the vocab sentence.

S10.why: Speaks to the person instead of the stiff noun 'Еднократно плащане', which reads like a bank form. 19 characters.

S11.why: One 'без' covers all three, which is how a Bulgarian would say it aloud. 'Регистрация' is the usual word for signing up to an account.

S12.why: Bulgarian buttons use the informal singular imperative, like the vocab's 'Продължи'. This is the phrase Bulgarian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action. 20 characters.

S13.why: The verbal noun of the same verb, as Bulgarian progress labels are written, ending in the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Imperative like the other buttons. 'Завинаги' carries the one-time payment in a word a buyer trusts, and nothing in it pushes. 19 characters plus the price.

S15.why: The same verb as S14. 'Завинаги' would go over the 14-character budget, and the row above already says the payment is one-time.

S16.why: The standard polite put-off in Bulgarian apps: it delays the purchase and does not refuse it.

S17.why: The plain imperative used for close buttons, the same form as 'Продължи' in the vocab.

S18.why: Warm with a little pride. 'Вече' (now, already) marks the change, and 'всичко' takes in all the new room. 18 characters.

S19.s: Благодаря ви за покупката. Така подкрепяте Кътлинг и човека, който сам го прави.
S19.back: Thank you for the-purchase. So you-support Cutling and the-person who alone it makes.
S19.why: Singular 'Благодаря', because 'Благодарим' would suggest a company. 'Сам го прави' says that one person makes it, without any sentimental wording.

S20.s: Добре дошли отново. Покупката ви е възстановена.
S20.back: Well come again. The-purchase your is restored.
S20.why: The usual Bulgarian welcome back, in plural-formal 'дошли', with the restore stated plainly.

S21.why: Passive, as a status read aloud, and it matches S5. The count form follows the 5.

S22.why: The vocab's own 'Кътлинги: %lld' pattern, so no count form is needed and it reads correctly for 1, 2, 5 and 21. The second number needs no noun.

S23.s: Кътлинг е отключен. Вече има място за %@ Кътлинга.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Now there-is room for 5 000 Cutlings.
S23.why: The app's name is masculine, so 'отключен'. The count form follows the number.

S24.why: Says what happened, with no subject to blame. 20 characters.

S25.s: App Store не е достъпен в момента. Опитайте отново след малко.
S25.back: App Store not is reachable at the-moment. Try again after a-little.
S25.why: App Store is treated as masculine ('достъпен'), as Bulgarians say it. 'След малко' is the natural word for shortly.

S26.s: App Store не потвърди тази покупка.
S26.back: App Store did-not confirm this purchase.
S26.why: One plain sentence that names the cause and blames nobody.

S27.s: Няма покупка на Кътлинг в Apple акаунта, с който сте влезли на това устройство.
S27.back: There-is-no purchase of Cutling in the-Apple account, with which you-have signed-in on this device.
S27.why: Opens with the fact, the way Bulgarian puts the main point first. 'Влезли' matches the vocab's 'влязло във вашия Apple акаунт'. 79 characters.

S28.s: Безплатната версия пази до %lld Кътлинга. Отключете Кътлинг веднъж и пазете колкото искате.
S28.back: The-free version keeps up-to 5 Cutlings. Unlock Cutling once and keep as-many-as you-want.
S28.why: Formal imperative because this is a full sentence spoken to the person; 'пази/пазете' is the same verb as the sheet. 88 characters.

S29.why: Under the 'Кътлинги' title the noun can be left out. 16 characters.

K1.why: 'Заети' (taken, like seats) says the slots are full and the items are untouched. 'Отключете' is the cue to tap. 33 characters.

M1.why: Bulgarian Mac window titles and menu commands use the verbal noun. 21 characters.

M2.why: Imperative as a button, the same verb as M1, with the ellipsis because it opens a window.

M3.why: A plain plural as a row label, using the vocab's item word.

M4.why: 'X от Y' is the compact Bulgarian number pair. 6 characters.

M5.why: Masculine agreement with the app's name. 18 characters.

M6.s: С една покупка Кътлинг се отключва на iPhone, iPad и Mac.
M6.back: With one purchase Cutling itself unlocks on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: The reflexive 'се отключва' is how Bulgarian describes what a purchase does. The list matches S8.

M7.s: Кътлинг е отключен на iPhone, iPad и Mac с този Apple акаунт.
M7.back: Cutling is unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple account.
M7.why: 'Този' points to the account signed in. 'Apple акаунт' is the vocab's term.

M8.s: Купихте Кътлинг, преди да стане безплатен, затова той остава отключен. Благодаря ви.
M8.back: You-bought Cutling before to become free, therefore it remains unlocked. Thank you.
M8.why: Says why it stays unlocked, then thanks them, with the same singular 'Благодаря' as S19. 'Безплатен' is masculine to agree with the app's name.
